name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Jasmine Clark's large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 97%
model.rationale: The district's +21 Democratic lean and an open seat held by Democrats make this safely Democratic; Clark's $1.6 million raised and $4.2 million in outside support against a lightly funded Republican reinforce that. Markets price a Democratic win at 97%, consistent with a Safe D call.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower race or a major outside-spending surge for Chavez would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is a heavily Democratic Atlanta-area seat with a +21 Democratic partisan lean. Incumbent Everton Blair is not on the ballot, leaving an open seat that Democrats have held. Democrat Jasmine Clark enters the general election with a strong financial position, having raised about $1.6 million and benefited from roughly $4.2 million in outside support, while Republican Jonathan Chavez reports little visible fundraising or outside spending.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the money gap. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97%. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling in the district.
